reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism operates through a two-stage process: first, an offline generation of item-to-item similarity mappings based on collective user behavior (purchases, ratings), encoding latent preferences into a structured adjacency graph. This graph is then queried during online inference to retrieve similar items for each known interest of a user. The retrieved lists are aggregated, scored, and ranked to produce a final recommendation set. The method assumes that users who interact with similar items share common preferences, enabling scalable personalization without explicit user profiling. Failure modes include sparsity in user-item interactions leading to unreliable similarity estimates, and cold-start scenarios where new users or items lack sufficient data for meaningful recommendations.
